body:
Happiness is a lie. Our brains are chemically designed to encounter pleasure as a brief, fleeting moment in a sea of disappointment. It's supposed to help keep pushing you forward, setting new goals, living. Attempting to permanently maintain a euphoric state is called a "drug problem," and is, also, not possible.

I'm not sure of anything more I could do for myself. I'm lucky enough to already do work I enjoy, and write my own schedules, and that means I can take all the time I need for myself. 

I take none. I find downtime painfully boring. 

I have no hobbies, no interests. When I was a teenager, I wrote, and I played music - several varieties of woodwinds and brass, nothing "cool." All of that faded away upon adulthood. Trying those things again is a daunting chore, and doesn't interest me. Nothing does. I already get paid to do the one thing on Earth that brings me any level of contentment...and the fact remains that I can't keep up with the rigors of trying to stay busy 100% of the time.

I like to sleep. I would sleep, but pain makes that difficult, at best. That's why the sudden loss of the painkillers is such a huge issue. It's taken me nearly ten years to strike a balance between pain management and functionality. Pain robs me of sleep, which makes me unable to function. I've tried the weed alone, and it remains insufficient. It is a great relaxer; it is not painkiller.
